key_insight: Halide ordering, not just random mixing, strongly controls miscibility and structural phase transitions in mixed halide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: Designing the halide and A-site composition can tune phase stability and suppress or induce temperature-sensitive transitions in perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for CsxRb1-xPbBr3yI3-3y, CsxRb1-xPbBr3yCl3-3y, and CsxRb1-xPbCl3yI3-3y.
Ran large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample both configurational and vibrational effects.
Compared miscibility gaps and phase-boundary shifts across compositions and temperatures.
evidence_signal: Simulations show miscibility gaps in all three binary halide systems, with layered halide ordering above the gap and phase-transition shifts of up to 100 K in CsPbBr3yI3-3y.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on MLIP accuracy and the studied composition/temperature range, so transfer to other chemistries or processing conditions should be validated.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
